This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 17-08-2021 at about 9.31 a.m., the Petitioner was riding her scooter bearing No.KA-02-JB-6523 from Nagarabhavi towards outer ring road via Mariyanpanapalya, when she reached Jagajyothi layout bus stop, the car bearing KA-02-AF-4884 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the scooter.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Aryan hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter shifted to Hosmat hospital, wherein she was treated as an inpatient.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was working as Head Mistress and earning Rs.1,02,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, she has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

4. It is the further case of the petitioner that the Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. Upon service of notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate objections to the main petition.

6. Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further he contended that the accident was caused solely due to negligence of the petitioner herself who was riding the motor cycle and not due to the negligence on the part of driver of the car.
Further contended that the car was insured with the 2nd respondent.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

7. Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Hemavathi vs Suresh N on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120420915/
2 offending car.
Further it contended that the accident was caused solely due to negligence of the petitioner herself who was riding the motor cycle and not due to the negligence on the part of driver of the car.
Further it contended that owner of the insured car has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent.

Further it contended that the driver of the Car was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and the owner of the car entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid driving licence.
It admitted the validity of the insurance to the offending car as on the date of accident subject to terms and conditions of policy and provisions of MV Act.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
8. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 17.08.2021 at about 9.30 a.m. near Jagajyothi Layout bus stop, Old ring road,
Mariyappanapalya, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing KA-02-AF-4884?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?

3. What Order or Award?
9.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.18.
Thereafter, the petitioner got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked document as per Ex.P.19 to 24 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondents have not adduced any evidence.

10. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and Respondents and on perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 11. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 17-08-2021 at about 9.30 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Regn.KA-02-AF- 4884 by its driver.

12. On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent Hemavathi vs Suresh N on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120420915/
3 driving of the driver of car bearing Regn.KA-02-AF-4884 by its driver.
13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, she got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-18.
She has re-iterated the Petition averments in her chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to 14 are the certified copies of FIR, complaint, Accident information report, Spot Mahazar,
Spot sketch, notice, statement of witnesses, IMV report, Wound certificate, notice issued U/s 133 of MV Act, reply to the said notice, Indemnity bond and charge sheet.
Ex.P.15 is the discharge summary.
Ex.P.16 is the Certificate issued by the Hospital, Ex.P.17 is the IT returns and Ex.P.18 is the copy of insurance policy.

14. Upon going through Ex.P.1 & 2 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Kamakshipalya Traffic Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of car bearing Regn.KA-02-AF-4884 for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
338 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Accident information report.
Ex.P.4 and 5 are the Spot Mahazar and spot sketch which show that the Panchanama has been drawn and sketch has been prepared at the spot in the presence of witnesses.

The sketch further shows that the petitioner was proceeding on extreme left side of the road and the driver of the offending car changed his lane from middle of the road to left side and hit the scooter.
Ex.P.7 and 8 are the statements of witnesses, they show that the witnesses before the IO stated about the accident as narrated by the petitioner in her petition.
Ex.P.9 is the IMV report, which show that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects and also justify the fact of involvement of vehicle in question in the accident.
It further disclose that the offending vehicle damaged front right side bumper.
Thereby the IMV report also supported the contents of other documents.
The document Ex.P.10 is the wound certificate, which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P.11 is the notice issued U/s 133 of MV Act and Ex.P.12 is the reply given to notice, which shows that the RC owner/respondent No.1 has admitted that the accused was the driver of the offending car at the time of accident.
Ex.P.13 is the Indemnity bond.

The document Ex.P.14 is the certified copy of Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation,
the PSI of Kamakshipalya Traffic Police Station has Charge- sheeted the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
15.

Further, Petitioner examined Dr.Krishan Prasad as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P.19 to 24 i.e., out patient and in patient case sheets and X-rays and X-rays reports.
16.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination, P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
17. In the cross-examination, P.W.2 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has assessed only physical disabilities and not functional disabilities.
He has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
18. The Respondents have not chosen to adduce any rebuttal evidence.
Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore,

sentences.text: having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No.KA-02-AF-4884 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
19. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
20. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 47 years.
She has not produced any documents to prove her age.
But as per police and medical documents, the age of the petitioner is shown as 47 years.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 47 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
21. Further, the petitioner has averred that she was working as Head Mistress and was earning Rs.1,02,000/- per month.
In this regard, she has produced Ex.P.17 IT returns acknowledgment for the year 2021-2022.
Wherein, her gross income per anuum is shown as Rs.8,50,340/- and her income tax was deducted Rs.85,871/- p.a.
After deducting the tax her income would be Rs.764,469/-.
If the said amount divides for 12 months it would be Rs.63,705/-.

In the said amount if professional tax of Rs.200/-p.m is deducted it would be Rs.63,500/- Therefore, Rs.63,505/- p.m.
is taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
22. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
23.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, she has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.10
Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Left elbow fracture dislocation with left proximal ulna fracture and radial head fracture.

Wherein,
the Doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner and period spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24.
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her she was in hospital for 3 days, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
As per the evidence of PW.2 doctor, the injuries are healed.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

sentences.text:
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
25.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in her evidence that she was admitted as an inpatient from 17-08-2021 to 19-08-2021 at Hosmat hospital.
The discharge summary of the petitioner also proves the same.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.Krishan Prasad has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 3 days.
26. It assumes importance to note that the petitioner is government teacher, hence she get earned leave and there is no evidence regarding LWA (leave without allowances).
Hence she had no loss during the laid up period.
Such being the case, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to get the compensation in this head.

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and she was admitted in the hospital for 3 days as an inpatient, and under went surgery and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
28. The Petitioner, in her petition stated that she has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
But she has not produced any medical bills and categorically admitted in her cross-examination that the amount incurred towards medical expenses has been reimbursed.
Hence, though she has stated to have spent sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses, she is not entitled for medical expenses under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
29. The petitioner has admitted in her cross examination that now she is drawing gross salary of Rs.82,000/- p.m. and no deduction in her salary due to the accident.
It means she is continuing her job even after the accident.
If this factor is taken into consideration, it is clear that the result of accident has no impact on the earning of the petitioner from her avocation.
This factor also justifies that as a result of accident PW.1 has not sustained any financial loss.
At this juncture it is profitable to refer the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2010 Kar 2439 Subash Vs The New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Rep.by its Manager & ors.

sentences.text: Re- Point 1:

As rightly pointed out by learned counsel appearing for Insured, the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding compensation towards loss of future income, resulting in serious miscarriage of justice, when in fact, the claimant has been continues in the service, then, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any loss of future income under this head.

VII COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
30.
The petitioner has not deposed anything about future medical expenses.
PW.2 doctor in his evidence deposed that the petitioner requires Rs.70,000/- for removal of implants and she will need a radial head after 10-15 years which will cost Rs.2,00,000/-.
But he is not the treated doctor and the treated doctor in the discharge summery, did not mention any thing about want of radial head after 10-15 years and there is no estimation in this regard.
But one thing is clear implants are in situ as per the Ex.P.24 X-ray report.
Definitely implants should be removed and it require, which will cost some amount and the same may vary from hospital to hospital.
In general for future medical expenses i.e., removal of implants it is necessary to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
31.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.
Medical expenses NIL 5. Loss of income during the -NIL- laid up period 6. Loss of Future income -NIL- 7.

Future medical expenses Rs. 50,000/-
Total Rs.1,48,000/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.1,48,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text: Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing KA-02-AF-4884.

There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
33. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 & 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.1,48,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
